races.name: CopyBet Supporting UK Horse Racing Amateur Jockeys' Handicap Chase (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Mt Fugi Park
runners_data.note: Prominent runner returning to form in first-time blinkers, 37 days since falling when going well at Carlisle, good ground suits.
runners_data.comment: Seemed to be running well before falling last time; remains on last winning mark
runners_data.spotlight: Disappointed on first two starts this season but seemed to be running well in first-time blinkers (retained) before falling at Carlisle (3m, good to soft) last month; remains on same mark as for last spring's good-ground win there and has top amateur Gina Andrews booked here; might be the answer.

runners_data.name: Knockanore
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse disappointed since big Eider Chase win but showed signs of life last time, needs strong pace to be effective.
runners_data.comment: Latest hurdle run was small step back in right direction; on dangerous chase mark
runners_data.spotlight: Generally very disappointing since winning last season's Eider Chase at Newcastle (4m1f, good to soft) by 16l but took small step back in right direction when fourth over hurdles last month (wore first-time blinkers) and is too well handicapped to rule out on this return to chasing; usual cheekpieces back on.

runners_data.name: Hurricane Bay
runners_data.note: Front-runner well handicapped on good-ground form but out of sorts recently, 31 days off may have freshened him up.
runners_data.comment: Sure to appreciate this ease in grade but needs to turn a corner
runners_data.spotlight: Well handicapped if judged on his two good-ground wins in cheekpieces last spring (2m7f/2m5f) but has been out of form (in various headgear) in recent months; sure to appreciate this ease in grade but needs to turn a corner; cheekpieces refitted.

runners_data.name: No But I Will
runners_data.note: Front-runner who won stable debut for Jessica Milly Smith, ran decent fourth fresh from break, visor applied.
runners_data.comment: Won on stable debut in December and also ran well when reappearing last month; a possible
runners_data.spotlight: Just held on to make winning stable debut under Jessica Milly Smith at Fakenham (2m5f, soft) in December and returned from break with fairly good fourth at Wetherby (2m3f, good to soft) last month; will also be suited by today's trip-and-ground combination; no surprise if he features.

runners_data.name: Giovanni Change
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with excellent course record (six wins), inconsistent but won well here last month off current mark.
runners_data.comment: Inconsistent nowadays but won last month and is sure to be suited by return to this track
runners_data.spotlight: Inconsistent in recent years and no longer the force of old but kept on well to score at Wetherby (3m, good) last month, and this six-time course winner is sure to be suited by the return to this track.

runners_data.name: Ladronne
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse in excellent form for new stable with two wins this season, veteran needs every yard of the trip, tongue-tie applied.
runners_data.comment: Veteran who has looked as good as ever for his new stable this season, winning twice
runners_data.spotlight: Veteran who has looked as good as ever for his new stable this season, winning twice (2m5f/3m1f); probably doesn't have much margin for error off current mark but reverts to chasing after a respectable hurdle run and is suited by this C&D.

races.paceDynamic: Hurricane Bay and No But I Will will force an honest gallop from the start, with Hurricane Bay's front-running style clashing against No But I Will's similar tactics. Giovanni Change and Mt Fugi Park will track prominently behind the leaders, while Knockanore and Ladronne will settle towards the rear as hold-up horses. The sustained pace over 3m on good ground will create a true test of stamina, with the race likely developing into a war of attrition from halfway. This honest gallop strongly favours prominent racers and hold-up horses who can finish, while pure front-runners may pay for early exertions.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Leaders Duel Early
scenarios.trigger: If Hurricane Bay and No But I Will engage in a pace battle from the start
scenarios.body: The sustained gallop will exhaust both leaders, setting up the race perfectly for Knockanore and Ladronne to deliver their trademark late challenges. The veteran Ladronne looks particularly well-suited to capitalize on a strong pace having shown excellent form this season.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Moderate Honest Pace
scenarios.trigger: If Hurricane Bay or No But I Will takes a clear lead while the other settles
scenarios.body: The leader will control the tempo allowing prominent racers to travel comfortably before launching their challenge. Giovanni Change's course expertise (six wins here) and Mt Fugi Park's return to form become decisive factors.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front Runner Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If Hurricane Bay breaks clear early and the field allows him an easy lead
scenarios.body: His proven ability on good ground over similar distances could see him dictate throughout and prove hard to peg back. No But I Will's similar style means she's best placed to give chase if the pace becomes tactical.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Crawling Early Pace
scenarios.trigger: If both leaders are restrained early creating a slowly-run affair
scenarios.body: The race becomes a sprint finish where class tells, favoring the highest-rated Mt Fugi Park and in-form Giovanni Change. The lack of a strong gallop negates the stamina advantage of the hold-up horses.

watchPoints.text: Hurricane Bay and No But I Will could neutralize each other if they engage in early speed duel
Mt Fugi Park needs to settle better than recent starts to be effective in first-time blinkers
Knockanore requires a genuinely-run race to show his best after recent disappointing efforts
Giovanni Change's course expertise could prove decisive if race develops into battle from halfway
Ladronne may need luck in running from rear given small field size limiting cover options

races.name: First Past The Post At CopyBet Mares' Maiden Hurdle (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Diamonds Galore
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with strong recent hurdle form, suited by the expected pace scenario and proven at this trip
runners_data.comment: Not herself in valuable race last month; sets clear standard on earlier form
runners_data.spotlight: Runner-up on first three hurdling starts this season, losing out only narrowly on handicap debut at Ludlow (2m, soft; front pair clear) in February; clearly not herself when pulled up in valuable series final last month but should be fine on the forecast good ground here and will be hard to beat if back on song.

runners_data.name: Briery Rose
runners_data.note: Hold-up type returning from 38-day break, needs the pace to develop to be effective from rear
runners_data.comment: Made quite promising bumper debut in 2024 but returned from layoff with a lesser effort
runners_data.spotlight: Out of connections' smart jumper Briery Belle; not beaten far when fifth of 13 in Uttoxeter bumper in December 2024 but returned from long layoff with less encouraging bumper run last month; improvement required.

runners_data.name: Georgia's Charm
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse who requires a strong gallop to show her closing kick, struggles if pace is too sedate
runners_data.comment: Second hurdle run was much better than the first; another step forward is needed, though
runners_data.spotlight: Placed in two bumpers in 2024 and bettered inauspicious stable/hurdle debut when fifth of 12 at Ludlow (2m, good) last month; needs another step forward to play anything more than a minor role here, though.

runners_data.name: Chatty Girl
runners_data.note: Prominent racer who has found only one better in recent starts, well-positioned for the likely tempo
runners_data.comment: Bumper winner who made the frame on three of first four hurdling starts; in the mix again
runners_data.spotlight: Dug deep to win soft-ground Newbury bumper on debut last season and has made the frame on three of her four hurdling starts this term; does not appear to be making any progress but ought to be on the premises here.

runners_data.name: Pour Tout Le Monde
runners_data.note: Natural front-runner making hurdling debut after 519-day absence, wears hood for first time
runners_data.comment: Showed only minor promise in bumpers in 2024; makes hurdle debut after long absence
runners_data.spotlight: Not beaten far in her first two bumpers in 2024 but finished down the field on her latest outing, and this hurdling debut comes after a 519-day absence; hood refitted.

runners_data.name: Flying Pimpernel
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse whose recent hurdle form has been disappointing over shorter trips
runners_data.comment: Placed in two of her three bumpers last year but first two hurdle runs were disappointing
runners_data.spotlight: Placed in two of her three bumpers last year but both hurdle runs last month (1m7f/2m3f) were disappointing; still has plenty of time to get her act together over jumps but arrives here with quite a bit to prove.

runners_data.name: Curious Mrs Fox
runners_data.note: Hold-up type prone to fading in finish, needs everything to fall right from the rear
runners_data.comment: 0-25 on the Flat; recent hurdling debut was respectable but she has a lot to find here
runners_data.spotlight: Lowly rated Flat maiden; seemed to take pretty well to hurdling when respectable fourth at Newcastle (2m4f, good to soft) a fortnight ago but has quite a lot to find here.

races.paceDynamic: Pour Tout Le Monde will likely lead or share the early pace with Diamonds Galore and Chatty Girl both racing prominently, creating a relatively sedate early tempo given the small field and lack of confirmed speed horses. The hold-up quartet of Briery Rose, Georgia's Charm, Flying Pimpernel and Curious Mrs Fox will be bunched towards the rear, relying on the pace to develop. With only one natural front-runner and several prominent racers not needing to be aggressive early, this sets up as a steady gallop that will quicken from the home turn. This race shape clearly favours the prominent racers who can position handy and have first run on the held-up horses when the pace lifts.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prominent Racers Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace stays moderate as expected with Pour Tout Le Monde leading unchallenged
scenarios.body: Diamonds Galore and Chatty Girl can travel smoothly in behind and kick clear when the tempo increases, while the hold-up horses struggle to make up ground from off the pace. The front three have the race sewn up before the closers can get involved.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Early Pace Collapse
scenarios.trigger: If Pour Tout Le Monde fails to lead effectively or goes too slowly early
scenarios.body: The race becomes a crawl that turns into a sprint, suiting the hold-up horses who can use their turn of foot. Briery Rose and Flying Pimpernel benefit most from the tactical nature this creates.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Strong Gallop Throughout
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent racers push Pour Tout Le Monde into a genuine gallop from early
scenarios.body: The sustained pace sets up perfectly for the hold-up horses to close late as the leaders tire. Georgia's Charm and Curious Mrs Fox can pick up the pieces in the final furlong.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Front Runner Wire-to-Wire
scenarios.trigger: If Pour Tout Le Monde gets an uncontested lead and stays on strongly
scenarios.body: The returning mare uses her 519-day break positively and holds off all challengers with a bold front-running display. Her early positioning proves decisive in a race where the hold-up horses can't get to her.

watchPoints.text: Pour Tout Le Monde's fitness after 519 days off could see her fold quickly if the prominent racers apply pressure
If the early pace is too slow it will negate the advantages of Diamonds Galore and Chatty Girl's handy positions
Georgia's Charm and Flying Pimpernel need the leaders to go a strong gallop to bring their closing kicks into play
Briery Rose showed little on return from long layoff last time and may need this run despite the yard's confidence
The small field of seven could lead to a tactical affair that doesn't suit the natural running styles

races.name: Safer Gambling At CopyBet Maiden Hurdle (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Plains Drifter
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with strong recent form including second to a Grade 2 winner, perfectly positioned to exploit weak pace-setting from ideal stalking position.
runners_data.comment: Second to smart rival over C&D on hurdle debut and placed again twice since; respected
runners_data.spotlight: Second to subsequent Grade 2 winner Montemares over C&D (good to soft) on hurdle debut in December and also placed on both subsequent outings, latterly when back here last month; respected.

runners_data.name: Jimmy Hurdstrom
runners_data.note: Prominent style with highest RPR of 127 and good going form, though 37 days off may need consideration for peak sharpness.

runners_data.name: Manalishi
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse returning after 136 days which is a significant concern, but has shown ability on good ground in limited appearances.
runners_data.comment: Second in a bumper; made jumping errors when well-held third on hurdle debut; can improve
runners_data.spotlight: Second on bumper debut at Chepstow (good) last April; made jumping errors when well-held when third in Doncaster novice hurdle (2m, soft) in November but has plenty of scope for improvement if he finds some fluency on this return to better ground, and his pedigree suggests the new trip will suit.

runners_data.name: Dontelimurnamepike
runners_data.note: Prominent 4-year-old getting weight allowance, but form against own age group suggests he may struggle against these older, more experienced rivals.
runners_data.comment: Showed minor promse against own age-group on last two starts; improvement needed here
runners_data.spotlight: Showed minor promise against own age-group on last two outings, more recenty when keeping on steadily for never-dangerous fifth at Wetherby (2m, soft; ride attracted stewards' attention) in January; needs significant improvement here, though.

runners_data.name: Sims' Law
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner with very poor form and tendency to fade, making him vulnerable unless the pace completely collapses.
runners_data.comment: With a good stable but struggled on his first two appearances
runners_data.spotlight: Half-brother to stable's useful jumper Coeur Serein but struggled (albeit on soft ground) on his first two appearances (2m/2m4f).

runners_data.name: Ebony Ebbs
runners_data.note: Confirmed leader with weak form and fade tendency, wearing tongue-tie for first time but 200-1 last time suggests limited ability.
runners_data.comment: Well beaten in both bumpers and when 200-1 for last month's hurdling debut
runners_data.spotlight: Well beaten in both bumpers and when 200-1 for last month's hurdling debut (2m3f).

races.paceDynamic: Ebony Ebbs will take the field along as the sole confirmed front runner, but given her weak form and tendency to fade, she's unlikely to set anything more than a moderate gallop. Plains Drifter, Jimmy Hurdstrom and Dontelimurnamepike will track close behind in prominent positions, with the hold-up pair Manalishi and Sims' Law dropping in behind. With only six runners and a modest pace-setter, this will develop into a tactical affair where the prominent racers can position perfectly without pressure. The lack of sustained early pace and small field size heavily favours prominent runners who can control their position and have the class edge over the likely weak leader.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If Ebony Ebbs sets only a moderate pace as expected and fades from 2f out.
scenarios.body: Plains Drifter and Jimmy Hurdstrom can position ideally behind the weakening leader and use their superior class ratings (OR 115/120) to pull clear. Both have the tactical speed and recent form to capitalize on perfect positioning in a slowly-run race.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Success
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses completely in the final half-mile with Ebony Ebbs stopping.
scenarios.body: Manalishi can use his hold-up style to sweep past tired leaders, especially with his proven good ground form. The collapse would bring his 136-day absence into less significance as stamina becomes key over pure race fitness.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Upset From Behind
scenarios.trigger: If both Plains Drifter and Jimmy Hurdstrom get trapped behind the fading Ebony Ebbs on the rail.
scenarios.body: Dontelimurnamepike could capitalize from a wide position with his prominent style, while the class horses struggle for room. His 4-year-old allowance and Jamie Hamilton's 5lb claim would provide crucial weight relief in a tactical finish.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If Ebony Ebbs stops abruptly early and no other horse wants to make the running.
scenarios.body: The race becomes a crawl where even Sims' Law could benefit from his hold-up style despite poor form. In a messy, tactical affair, any horse getting first run could prevail if the others are caught napping.

watchPoints.text: Plains Drifter and Jimmy Hurdstrom getting perfect stalking positions behind Ebony Ebbs could lock out the finish if the pace is moderate.
Ebony Ebbs stopping abruptly in the straight could cause traffic problems for horses following too closely behind the pace.
Manalishi's jumping accuracy after 136 days off as errors at Doncaster showed he can be vulnerable when rusty.
Shane Quinlan's 3lb claim and tongue-tie first time on Ebony Ebbs suggests connections think she needs every assistance.
The small field of six making this more tactical than usual, with positioning at the final turn becoming crucial for the hold-up horses.

races.name: CopyBet Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Snapius
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner faces significant task from rear given likely steady pace, though 27-day break freshens him up
runners_data.comment: Cosily ended a losing run at Huntingdon latests; back up 6lb but not taken lightly
runners_data.spotlight: Ended a losing run in 2m4f handicap at Huntingdon 27 days ago; back up 6lb but had something to spare there so not taken lightly.

runners_data.name: Hans Lippershey
runners_data.note: Natural front-runner will get easy lead, key question is whether he can sustain kick when challenged
runners_data.comment: Good second at Fakenham latest; very much one to consider in his bid for a maiden win
runners_data.spotlight: Fair bumper performer who has matched that form in this sphere, still not foot perfect when a good second of five in 2m Fakenham novice last month; this return to further should suit so he's very much one to consider, especially if hurdling better.

runners_data.name: Play Pretend
runners_data.note: 174-day absence major concern for hold-up horse who needs things to fall right from the back
runners_data.comment: Very good second at Worcester in October; this course winner must enter calculations
runners_data.spotlight: Scored at Worcester (2m) last July and posted a very good second of 11 in 2m4f handicap there when last seen out in October; this course winner has gone well fresh so must enter calculations.

runners_data.name: Lord Chamberlain
runners_data.note: Progressive type with tactical speed to sit handy, 5lb claimer reduces effective weight burden
runners_data.comment: Greatly advanced form on h'cap debut with easily Hereford win; major shout under 7lb pen
runners_data.spotlight: Fair maiden on the Flat who greatly advanced his form on his handicap hurdle debut when scoring easily at Hereford (2m) eight days ago; major shout under a 7lb penalty.

runners_data.name: Caramelo Rapido
runners_data.note: Hold-up style completely wrong for this race shape, needs much stronger pace than anticipated
runners_data.comment: Beat only one in 2m Hexham handicap 20 days ago; needs to bounce back
runners_data.spotlight: Opened his account at Doncaster (2m) in February but he beat only one in 2m Hexham handicap 20 days ago; needs to bounce back.

runners_data.name: Assorda
runners_data.note: Another hold-up runner poorly positioned for steady gallop, 12-month absence compounds difficulties
runners_data.comment: Has shown little after 12 months off in handicaps at Catterick and Sedgefield this year
runners_data.spotlight: Scored twice (at up to 2m3f) in early 2025 but she's shown little after 12 months off in a pair of handicaps at Catterick and Sedgefield for her current yard this year; others appeal more.

runners_data.name: Ruler Legend
runners_data.note: 7lb penalty harsh but prominent style suits, course winner with tactical advantage from forward position
runners_data.comment: Readily gained first win in over two years here recently; can go well under 7lb penalty
runners_data.spotlight: Readily gained a first victory in over two years when capitalising on a reduced mark in 2m handicap here nine days ago; carries a 7lb penalty but can go well again.

runners_data.name: Nitty Gritty
runners_data.note: 109-day layoff concern for horse who needs to be closer than usual hold-up style suggests
runners_data.comment: Best effort for current yard when fifth at Wetherby on Boxing Day; not out of things
runners_data.spotlight: A fairly useful 2m4f hurdles scorer for Joseph O'Brien; recorded much his best effort for his current yard when fifth of ten  in 2m4f handicap at Wetherby on Boxing Day; not out of things if building on that after a break.

runners_data.name: Ever Ready
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner lacks pace and class to overcome tactical disadvantage from rear position
runners_data.comment: Remains winless and comes here on back of a below-par sixth at Southwell three weeks ago
runners_data.spotlight: Remains winless and she comes here on the back of a below-par sixth in 2m4f Southwell handicap three weeks ago; others are preferred.

runners_data.name: Ambassador
runners_data.note: Aging performer whose prominent style gives chance despite poor recent form trend
runners_data.comment: Won at Cartmel in August but his form has nosedived since
runners_data.spotlight: Back to winning ways at Cartmel (2m1f) in August but his form has nosedived since, beating just one after a lay-off at Sedgefield (2m1f) 13 days ago.

runners_data.name: Times A Wastin
runners_data.note: Tongue-tie addition interesting but hold-up style faces uphill task in steady-run race
runners_data.comment: Rejoined former stable after beating one at Warwick (for Tony Carroll) in February
runners_data.spotlight: Still to register a victory and he has rejoined former stable after beating only one in 2m3f Warwick handicap for Tony Carroll in February; tongue-tie goes on here.

races.paceDynamic: Hans Lippershey will take them along from the front with minimal pressure, likely joined by Ruler Legend and Ambassador in the early stages. With most of the field being hold-up horses (Snapius, Play Pretend, Lord Chamberlain, Caramelo Rapido, Assorda, Ever Ready, Times A Wastin), the pace will be steady rather than frantic through the middle sections. The lack of genuine pace pressure means the tempo will be manageable, setting up a finish where stamina and tactical positioning from mid-division matter most. This race shape strongly favours prominent runners and those who can sit handy, as the hold-up brigade will have too much work to do from the rear.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Uncontested Lead Sustains
scenarios.trigger: If Hans Lippershey gets an easy time in front without pressure from the prominent runners.
scenarios.body: The steady gallop plays perfectly into his hands as he conserves energy for a strong finish. His recent Fakenham second suggests he has the class edge when not having to fight for position early.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Battle Unfolds
scenarios.trigger: If Ruler Legend and Ambassador press Hans Lippershey early, creating genuine pace pressure.
scenarios.body: The increased tempo stretches the field and brings stamina into play over this 2m2½f trip. Those sitting just off the pace in fourth or fifth can time their runs perfectly as the leaders tire.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Charge Succeeds
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses completely in the middle sections, creating a sprint finish.
scenarios.body: The lack of early pace allows the back markers to close dramatically in the final half-mile. This scenario needs everything to fall right for the hold-up horses who must navigate traffic and find racing room.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Chaos Benefits Outsider
scenarios.trigger: If early fallers or interference disrupts the natural order and creates tactical confusion.
scenarios.body: The race becomes a lottery where horses getting clear runs at the right moment can capitalize on others' misfortune. Lower-rated runners with tactical pace can steal it.

watchPoints.text: Hans Lippershey getting uncontested lead through first mile - will be very hard to peg back if unchallenged
Lord Chamberlain's inexperienced 5lb claimer handling tactical battle if race develops into early skirmish
Play Pretend's jumping after 174-day break - any mistakes from rear position will end chances immediately
Ruler Legend handling 7lb penalty on quick 9-day turnaround after recent course success
Early pace development between Hans Lippershey and prominent runners determining entire race dynamic

runners_data.spotlight: Pulled up in two handicap chases this season (2m5f/2m) and now 0-8 under all codes; sports first-time cheekpieces here; 1lb out of the weights; leap of faith required to support him.

races.paceDynamic: Catchim and O'Grady's Hill will contest the early lead, with both confirmed front runners likely to set an honest gallop from the start. Grain Trade will sit prominently just behind this duo, while the hold-up horses Jiair Madrik and Chateau Du Lys will need to be positioned closer than usual in this small field. With two keen front runners likely to ensure a solid pace throughout, the race sets up to favor the prominent racers who can track the pace without getting embroiled in the early battle.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Honest Pace Benefits Tracker
scenarios.trigger: If Catchim and O'Grady's Hill set a fair tempo without killing each other
scenarios.body: Grain Trade can sit in the perfect stalking position behind the leaders and time his challenge. His class advantage over the field becomes decisive when the front pair tire approaching the last fence.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If Catchim gets first run on O'Grady's Hill and establishes a clear lead
scenarios.body: His superior class tells as he can dictate terms without serious pressure until late. The hold-up horses find the pace too honest to mount effective challenges from the back.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Strikes Late
scenarios.trigger: If the two front runners go too fast early and compromise each other
scenarios.body: Jiair Madrik benefits from the strong pace as the leaders weaken approaching the final fence. His recent decent effort at Bangor suggests he retains enough ability despite being 0-5 over fences.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Weak Pace Favors Closer
scenarios.trigger: If both front runners show early restraint and create a tactical affair
scenarios.body: O'Grady's Hill can utilize his 20lb weight advantage to stay closer to the pace throughout. The race becomes a sprint finish where his fresher legs and lighter burden prove decisive.

watchPoints.text: Catchim and O'Grady's Hill could go too fast early and set it up for the closers if they get competitive
Jiair Madrik needs to settle better than last time when he raced too freely at Bangor
Grain Trade's tongue-tie fitting suggests connections expect improved performance from his course winner
Greenways has first-time tongue-tie but his recent form is dire despite the handicapper's assistance
Chateau Du Lys sports first-time cheekpieces after two pull-ups but faces a tough task from 133 days off

races.name: Market Rasen Racecourse Caravan & Touring Park Novices' Handicap Chase (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Southoftheborder
runners_data.note: Prominent runner who finally broke his chasing duck at Kempton and should track Cuban Court early but may lack the finishing kick to capitalize
runners_data.comment: Beat a next-time-out winner when scoring at Kempton last month; only 3lb higher here
runners_data.spotlight: Took nine attempts to open chasing account but the form of his win at Kempton (2m2f, good) three weeks ago was nicely boosted by the runner-up on Saturday, and this fellow is still on a good mark after a 3lb rise.

runners_data.name: Kayce Dutton
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist with dual course wins this season but inconsistency remains a major concern despite proven Market Rasen form
runners_data.comment: Dual course winner this season (2m5f/3m) but took inconsistent to rely upon heavily
runners_data.spotlight: Dual course winner this season (2m5f/3m); too inconsistent to rely upon heavily, though, and was no match for winner when second at Southwell (2m4f, good) a fortnight ago; swaps cheekpieces for first-time visor; others appeal more.

runners_data.name: Cuban Court
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner in excellent form with two wide-margin wins but rising weights and tactical disadvantage against this field composition
runners_data.comment: 3-4 over fences, the last two wins gained by wide margins in small fields at Doncaster
runners_data.spotlight: 3-4 over fences, the last two wins gained by wide margins in small fields at Doncaster (2m3f, good/good to soft); shooting up the weights but evidently in very good nick.

runners_data.name: Singapore Trip
runners_data.note: Recently returned to chasing with clear-cut Wetherby win showing renewed confidence and hold-up style suits this race shape perfectly
runners_data.comment: Has returned to chasing in recent weeks and was a clearcut winner at Wetherby last time
runners_data.spotlight: Five-time hurdle winner who has returned to chasing in recent weeks and was a clearcut winner at Wetherby (1m7f, good) on his latest outing; features prominently in calculations.

runners_data.name: Icare Colombe
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse whose cheekpieces have sparked improvement lately with 5-length course win last month proving his effectiveness here
runners_data.comment: Up in grade after last month's course win but further progress is possible
runners_data.spotlight: Not an instant success over fences this season but cheekpieces seem to have helped lately and he won by 5l off a reduced mark here (2m1f, good to soft) last month; moves up in grade today but should be fine over the longer trip and might use that recent success as a springboard.

races.paceDynamic: Cuban Court will lead from the start with his confirmed front-running style, setting a sustainable gallop over this 2m3f trip on good ground. With only Southoftheborder likely to press him early from a prominent position, Cuban Court should get an easy lead through the early stages. The lack of genuine pace pressure will allow the leader to dictate terms, but also gives the hold-up quartet (Kayce Dutton, Singapore Trip, Icare Colombe) time to organize their challenges from off the pace. This race shape clearly favors closers and hold-up horses who can capitalize on a modest early gallop and strong-traveling position into the straight.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is truly modest and Cuban Court gets too easy a lead
scenarios.body: Cuban Court will have energy reserves but the hold-up horses will have maximum tactical advantage with plenty left for their finishing kicks. Singapore Trip or Icare Colombe can produce late surges that the front-runner cannot match.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Survives
scenarios.trigger: If Cuban Court maintains enough tempo to blunt the closers' kicks
scenarios.body: The leader's class and current form allow him to repel late challenges despite the tactical setup favoring his rivals. His wide-margin recent wins demonstrate he can sustain pressure when asked.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Runner Benefits
scenarios.trigger: If Southoftheborder tracks Cuban Court closely and inherits the lead late
scenarios.body: The prominent runner gets the best of both worlds - saving ground early while avoiding the traffic problems that could hinder the hold-up horses. Southoftheborder's recent Kempton win shows he can capitalize on favorable positioning.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Course Specialist Emerges
scenarios.trigger: If Kayce Dutton's dual course wins this season prove decisive
scenarios.body: The local knowledge and proven ability at Market Rasen overcome his inconsistency issues when the race develops to suit hold-up horses. His Southwell second shows current ability when conditions align.

watchPoints.text: Cuban Court sets the fractions - if he goes too slowly early he becomes vulnerable to multiple closers in the straight
Singapore Trip's jumping under pressure as he's recently returned to fences after hurdle success
Southoftheborder's positioning behind Cuban Court - needs to stay close enough to inherit but not get trapped
Kayce Dutton's inconsistency factor - has the course form but tendency to disappoint when fancied
The pace through the first mile will determine whether this becomes a sprint finish favoring the hold-up horses

races.name: Book Summer Plate Ladies Day Today Mares' Novices' Handicap Chase (Premier Handicap) (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Jasmine Bliss
runners_data.note: Front-runner with Listed form but 52 days off and faces another confirmed pace-setter in Bluey
runners_data.comment: Listed winner in February and second in Grade 2 Pendil later that month
runners_data.spotlight: Opened chasing account at second attempt, with Listed success at Huntingdon (2m4f, soft) in February, and was creditable second in Grade 2 Pendil at Kempton (2m4f, good to soft) later that month; still has potential over fences; respected on handicap return.

runners_data.name: Lunar Discovery
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse in prime form after December Chepstow win, should benefit from expected strong pace
runners_data.comment: Back in prime form at Chepstow in December but not quite as good last month, after a break
runners_data.spotlight: Seemingly back in prime form when beating a subsequent Cheltenham winner at Chepstow (2m3f, good to soft) in December but wasn't at same level when weakening third at Stratford (2m6f, good) last month, after a break, and needs that recent run to have brought her on.

runners_data.name: Ruby Island
runners_data.note: Proven closer who was third behind Jasmine Bliss at Huntingdon and won easily last time at Haydock
runners_data.comment: Third behind Jasmine Bliss in Listed contest in February and won a match race last month
runners_data.spotlight: Respectable third behind Jasmine Bliss in Huntingdon Listed contest (2m4f, soft) in February before comfortably doubling chase tally in Haydock match race (2m4f, good to soft) last month; 7lb better off with Jasmine Bliss today; likely contender.

runners_data.name: Molto Bene
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with good chase form, narrowly beaten in Listed company recently
runners_data.comment: 2-4 over fences; close second to a next-time-out winner last time; has a fighting chance
runners_data.spotlight: Launched chasing career with two wins in the autumn (2m4f/2m7f) and came second in two subsequent Listed races (hurdle/chase); lost out only narrowly to a next-time-out winner when back in a handicap at Leicester (2m4f, good to soft) last month and has a fighting chance here.

runners_data.name: Bluey
runners_data.note: Fellow front-runner with class edge, 59 days since last run but trainer in good form with 1/12 strike-rate

runners_data.name: All The Glory
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with mixed form but ran well behind Bluey at Windsor when 40-1
runners_data.comment: Has mixed record this season but her Windsor third in January brings her right into this
runners_data.spotlight: Has rather mixed record over fences this season but belied 40-1 odds when close third in valuable Windsor handicap (2m4f, soft) won by Bluey in January and last month's Cheltenham Festival defeat is easily excused; on good mark if on her mettle.

runners_data.name: She Is For Me Boys
runners_data.note: Prominent style, lowest rating but won on chase debut and gets significant weight relief
runners_data.comment: Yet to build upon promising chase debut in the autumn but still enters calculations
runners_data.spotlight: Created pretty good impression when winning on chase/handicap debut at Kempton (2m4f, good) in November; yet to build on that effort but ran quite well when third at Warwick (2m, good to soft) last month and ought to be better suited by today's trip-and-ground combination; 1lb wrong; could have a say.

runners_data.name: Epinephrine
runners_data.note: Unexposed over this trip, keeping-on second at Bangor suggests stamina will suit
runners_data.comment: Last month's Bangor second came in an run-of-the-mill handicap but she may yet do better
runners_data.spotlight: Last month's keeping-on second at Bangor (2m1f, good to soft) came in just a run-of-the-mill handicap and she's now 0-4 over fences but she's unexposed over this sort of trip and may still have a bigger run in her; unraced on ground quicker than good to soft.

races.paceDynamic: Jasmine Bliss and Bluey are both confirmed front-runners who will contest the early lead, creating an honest gallop from the outset. With two pace-setters likely to go at it, the tempo should be genuine throughout this 2m5½f trip at Market Rasen. The sustained pace will stretch the field and test stamina reserves in the closing stages. This race shape strongly favours hold-up horses like Lunar Discovery, Ruby Island and All The Glory who can pick up the pieces when the early leaders weaken.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Front Runners Collapse
scenarios.trigger: If Jasmine Bliss and Bluey go too hard early and tie up
scenarios.body: The strong pace will find both leaders out in the final half-mile, leaving the door open for closers to sweep past. Hold-up horses with tactical speed will have perfect conditions to unleash late runs.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Bluey Survives Battle
scenarios.trigger: If Bluey can see off Jasmine Bliss and maintain stamina
scenarios.body: Harry Cobden's mount has the class edge and better recent form to outlast her main pace rival. Her superior rating and tactical nous under pressure gives her the edge in a sustained duel.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Moderate Early Pace
scenarios.trigger: If both leaders go more conservatively than expected
scenarios.body: A steadier gallop would suit the prominent runners and allow more horses to stay in contention longer. This would bring the mid-pack horses like Molto Bene and She Is For Me Boys into the equation late.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Jasmine Bliss Wire-to-Wire
scenarios.trigger: If Jasmine Bliss can dictate terms and maintain her kick
scenarios.body: Paul O'Brien's mount could use her class to control the tempo and find enough in reserve. Her Listed win at Huntingdon shows she has the quality when things fall right.

watchPoints.text: Jasmine Bliss and Bluey could go too fast early given both are natural front-runners meeting for pace supremacy
Lunar Discovery needs the anticipated strong pace to materialize to be seen at best
All The Glory at big odds could outrun her price if the pace collapses as expected
She Is For Me Boys carries bottom weight but needs to build on her debut chase win
Track Molto Bene for market confidence given trainer Charlie Longsdon is 0/15 in last 14 days

races.name: CopyBet Daily Profit Boost Open National Hunt Flat Race (Category 1 Elimination) (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Denis The Badger
runners_data.comment: Third foal from an unraced dam; stable has only occasional bumper winners
runners_data.spotlight: Frontiersman gelding from an unraced dam; stable has only occasional bumper winners.

runners_data.name: Hillsteels Blue
runners_data.comment: Out of a hurdle-winning daughter of a French 2m2f Grade 3 winner; yard quiet in bumpers
runners_data.spotlight: Out of a hurdle-winning daughter of a French 2m2f Grade 3 winner; trainer has modest strike-rate in bumpers.

runners_data.name: Royal March
runners_data.comment: Out of a 2m4f hurdle winner; wily trainer's bumper horses are always worth a look
runners_data.spotlight: Third foal; dam 2m4f hurdle winner, sister to a 2m4f chase winner; wily trainer doesn't have many runners nowadays but his bumper horses are always worth a look.

runners_data.name: Sea Lord
runners_data.comment: Brother to a useful Flat winner; first National Hunt runner for respected Flat stable
runners_data.spotlight: Third foal; brother to 1m2f/1m4f AW winner Ocean Wave (RPR 92), half-brother to 1m AW winner Ocean Manifest (83); dam Listed-placed 8.6f/1m4f AW winner (95), half-sister to dam of French 1,000 Guineas/French Oaks winner La Cressonniere; first ever National Hunt runner for respected Flat trainer.

runners_data.name: Crystal Glade
runners_data.comment: Trainer is not prolific in bumpers but has done well with this filly's family
runners_data.spotlight: Seventh foal; half-sister to winners Rainyday Woman (Listed bumper/hurdle) and William Cody (2m4f chase); dam useful jumper; trainer is not prolific in bumpers but has done well with this filly's family.

runners_data.name: Popalot
runners_data.comment: Shaped with significant promise when third of five over C&D in November
runners_data.spotlight: Out of a bumper winner; shaped with significant promise when third of five in tactical contest over C&D (good to soft) in November, and the form has worked out quite well in the meantime; one to consider.

runners_data.name: Middlecliffe
runners_data.comment: Well beaten at triple-digit odds on both starts last month
runners_data.spotlight: Has some good jumpers in his family but was well beaten at triple-digit odds on both starts last month.

runners_data.name: Bite The Bullet
runners_data.comment: Stable usually does well in bumpers but this fellow struggled on last month's debut
runners_data.spotlight: Sprint bred on his dam's side; with a respected stable that generally does well in bumpers but struggled when 22-1 for debut at Huntingdon (2m, good to soft) in March and needs to take a big step forward.
